newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holzmann shares up after Transrapid news.
newsitem.headline: Holzmann shares up after Transrapid news.

text.p: Shares in Germany's largest construction group, Philipp Holzmann AG, rose strongly in pre-bourse trade on Friday after it confirmed that it and other builders were quitting the Transrapid rail project.
Holzmann shares rose 11 marks to 486 in IBIS electronic trade.

"It's a money pit project and the market so far thinks it is good for the construction groups to get out now," said one trader. "But there's still speculation they may return to the project in some form in the future."
Holzmann earlier confirmed that the construction groups in the Hamburg-Berlin rapid rail would be leaving the consortium set up to design and build the nine billion mark Transrapid rail project.
Holzmann told Reuters that the Transrapid consortium considered the costs associated with Holzmann, Hochtief AG and Bilfinger+Berger AG were too high.
The three builders had seen no room to reduce costs to the extent demanded by the other partners in the consortium.

The Transrapid project, which uses magnetic levitation technology, has come under criticism both as to whether there is sufficient demand for it in Germany and whether it can justify the six billion marks of state funding Bonn plans to offer for it.
Hochtief gained 64 pfennigs to 64 marks, while Bilfinger was not dealt in IBIS trade.
